ice_source: NOAA/NSIDC Sea Ice Concentration CDR G02202 v6, 25 km

corridors.label: A
corridors.name: Planned
corridors.rationale: The corridor the prototype has always shown, at the configured 80% working ice limit.

corridors.label: B
corridors.name: Conservative
corridors.rationale: Same ship and ice, limit tightened to 55%. Costs 0.08 days and ten extra legs — and raises the worst ice actually sampled along the line from 74% to 91%, because the router optimises on 5° cell means while this figure comes from 25 km pixels.

corridors.why: no route exists for this vessel on this mesh — Dijkstra could not connect the waypoints
corridors.label: C
corridors.name: Cautious
corridors.rationale: At a 45% limit no route to Bharati exists at all. Not slower — unreachable. Since 80% is an assumption rather than a certificated limit, this is where that assumption stops being survivable.

findings.finding: Solving for fuel instead of traveltime returns a byte-identical path at every ice limit tested.
findings.why: zero_currents is True and PolarRoute's wave-added-resistance function is dead code in 1.1.11, so fuel is a monotone function of time and there is no trade-off surface.
findings.consequence: Do not present fuel and time as two objectives until a current or wave field makes them diverge. ADR-021's unrun sweep would have found this.

findings.finding: Tightening the ice limit from 60% to 55% raises the worst ice sampled along the route from 74% to 91%.
findings.why: The router plans on 5° cellbox means; the published figure is sampled from 25 km pixels. A cell whose mean is under the limit can still contain pixels far above it.
findings.consequence: The 'heaviest ice on the route' number is not a quantity the router ever optimised against, and must not be presented as though it were.

findings.finding: Bharati is reachable at assumed limits of 50% and above, and unreachable at 45% and below.
findings.why: Dijkstra cannot connect the waypoints once too many cells close.
findings.consequence: Reachability of the destination rests on an assumed threshold with a cliff edge, not on a certificated limit.

caveat: Steaming time only. PolarRoute's wave-added-resistance function is dead code in this version, so sea state applies no speed or fuel penalty and every duration here is a lower bound.
